Background 2. Brief facts of the case culled from petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act would reveal that Sanjay Kumar driving motorcycle no. HR-36S-7864 on his way back to home had reached near the house of Manphool, Village Akheri Madanpur, Jhajjar on 17.12.2014 at around 5:45 pm when offending Truck No. HR-63B-0874 driven by R1/Sandeep from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner at very high speed hit his motorcycle forcefully as a result of which he fell on the road and sustained multiple injuries.

19. Section 166(2) of M.V. Act, 1988 provides that every application under sub-section (1) shall be made at the option of the claimant, either to the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area in which the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant MACT 544/16 Bimla Sharma Vs. Sandeep & Anr. Page No. 10 of 29 resides or carries on business or within the local limit of whose jurisdiction the defendant resides.

20. In the present case, petitioners have approached Claims Tribunal, South West Dwarka affirming residence at B/30, Dhansa Road, Gopal Nagar Extension, Najafgarh, Delhi whereas electricity bill of Plot No. 237/238, Block-B Nanda Enclave has been filed along with statements of neighbourers namely Sh. Daya Nand and Smt. Mukesh verifying their residence at House No. 237/238, Block-B Nanda Enclave.

Considering the fact that petition filed on 09.04.2015 is pending for more than 09 years whereas provisions under Chapter-XI and XII of the M.V. Act are benevolent legislation,
Courts are required to take the view that would promote the object of ameliorating pain and suffering of victims of road accident instead of returning the petition on the ground of territorial jurisdiction.

It is, therefore, held that petition under section 166 & 140 M.V. Act seeking compensation for death in motor vehicle accident at Nauganwa, Akheri Road, Jhajjar, Haryana is maintainable on the basis of verification report forwarded by SHO PS Najafgarh.

Act, 1988 provides that every application under sub-section (1) shall be made at the option of the claimant, either to the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area in which the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant MACT 544/16 Bimla Sharma Vs. Sandeep & Anr. Page No. 10 of 29 resides or carries on business or within the local limit of whose jurisdiction the defendant resides.
Considering the fact that petition filed on 09.04.2015 is pending for more than 09 years whereas provisions under Chapter-XI and XII of the M.V. Act are benevolent legislation,
Courts are required to take the view that would promote the object of ameliorating pain and suffering of victims of road accident instead of returning the petition on the ground of territorial jurisdiction.
25. Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court in Bimla Devi Vs. Punjab State, 2001 (1) RCR (Civil) 596 SC has held that MACT 544/16 Bimla Sharma Vs. Sandeep & Anr. Page No. 12 of 29 statement of witness cannot be discarded simply because the witness did not report the matter to the police.
26. Though, R1/Sandeep has been acquitted of the charge under section 279/304A IPC in the absence of sufficient evidence to establish death of Sanjay due to rash and negligent driving by accused, however, it is well settled law that acquittal in a criminal case has no bearing on the determination of negligence in claim proceedings and result of criminal case is inconsequential as Tribunal is expected to make independent inquiry to reach a conclusion as to whether negligence on the part of driver has been proved on the touchstone of preponderance of probability or not, rather than on proof of guilt beyond all reasonable doubt as held by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 8 of judgment titled Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shama Parveen & Ors.
28. It is important to bear in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible for the claimants who are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability as standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
29.
Similar ruling has been returned by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors.
2007 SCC Online Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
31. Hence in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is established that death of Sanjay Kumar has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending Truck No. HR-63B-0874 on the basis of site-plan, siezure memo & mechanical inspection report of Truck and motorcycle involved in the accident read with postmortem report of deceased mentioning cause of death as haemmorage and shock due to injury to vital organs which were antemotem in nature and sufficient to cause death in normal course of life.
In the facts and circumstances of the case and on the basis of evidence adduced on record it is established that death of Sanjay Kumar has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of Truck No. HR-63B-0874 by R1/Sandeep which vehicle was insured with R2/Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co.
